P: 1. Transfer to the emergency department immediately for spine assessment and urgent lumbar MRI; document exact onset of bladder and saddle symptoms and assess motor/sensory deficits without delaying transfer; explain possible nerve compression and need for urgent specialist decisions; avoid spinal manipulation or a routine wait-and-see plan.

2. Review fever, injection drug use, immune suppression and procedures; obtain urgent lumbar MRI and infection testing through the emergency team if indicated; explain that lack of fever alone cannot exclude serious spinal infection.

3. Ask cancer and constitutional history and obtain urgent imaging for neurologic compression; involve the relevant spine/oncology teams if supported; explain that malignancy is a possibility to assess, not a known result.
